title: Introduce tenant-scoped GPU NodeClass allocator and IAM credential broker for private installs
author: Diego Martinez
release_notes: Adds tenant-scoped GPU nodeclass allocator and an IAM credential broker. Migration tool migrates previous state to per-tenant partitions. No API surface changes for customers; requires ops coordination for state migration.
body:
Context and motivation: Private deployments require stronger isolation across tenants for GPU node allocation, IAM credential separation, and clean rollback semantics during upgrades. Current installer uses a shared nodepool TF module and a monolithic state file which complicates operator workflows when tenants cross-claim resources or when credential rotation is required. This PR introduces two coordinated Terraform modules and supporting migration tooling: (1) tenant-scoped gpu_nodeclass_allocator module that models GPU node classes as immutable "nodeclass" resources pinned per-tenant and per-az; (2) iam_credential_broker module that creates short-lived, auditable IAM credentials for node bootstrap and rotation with HSM-backed keys in supported environments. Additionally, a state-partitioner helper (go binary in tools/) performs an online-safe split of legacy state into per-tenant statefiles and updates backend locks to avoid double-apply races.

Design summary: - gpu_nodeclass_allocator: declares a nodeclass CRD-like Terraform resource that includes tenant_id, sku_profile, az_affinity, and lifecycle strategies (create-before-destroy, replacement grace period). The module emits mapping outputs used by the installer to construct node labels and taints. It also supports a policy flag allow_shared_pools when tenant isolation is not desired. - iam_credential_broker: issues one bootstrap credential per nodeclass with limited scopes and a rotate endpoint (via a simple controller manifest) for environments that support webhook-based rotation. Credentials are recorded in audit logs and optionally provisioned into Vault or a KMS secret engine. - state-partitioner (tools/state_partitioner): scans the legacy tfstate, computes resource sets per tenant using tags/metadata (fallback to naming heuristics), writes new per-tenant statefiles into the existing backend namespace, acquires locks during cut-over, and emits a migration plan. The partitioner is idempotent and supports a dry-run mode for operator validation.

Migration plan: 1) Dry-run using state-partitioner --dry-run to generate migration plan and mapping; 2) Apply iam_credential_broker in a canary tenant to verify credential rotation and node bootstrap; 3) Run state-partitioner for tenant group A with lock acquisition window during off-peak; 4) Apply gpu_nodeclass_allocator against per-tenant statefiles and reconcile existing nodepools; 5) Monitor metrics and rollback by re-merging per-tenant state into legacy file using partitioner --rollback.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for Terraform modules (module-level acceptance tests) included in tests/ with mocked provider state. - End-to-end staging run in our internal on-prem lab: created 3 tenant-specific nodeclasses, validated autoscaler bindings and GVNIC interface attachment, verified IAM credential rotation via the broker controller. - CI: initial test matrix failed on a linting rule for module variable naming; updated variable names and re-ran. Final CI run was green across terraform validate, kitchen tests, and the private-installer integration pipeline.

Security considerations: Credentials are least-privilege and TTL-bound; default rotation is 24h but configurable. The broker can be configured to write secrets to Vault or a KMS-backed secret store only. Audit hooks are added to the module outputs to support operator auditing.

Rollout and rollback: The modules are non-breaking by default; operator must opt-in to per-tenant partitioning. The state-partitioner includes a safe rollback that rehydrates legacy state and re-acquires backend locks. We recommend a staged rollout: canary tenant -> small cohort -> full rollout with 48h monitoring window.

Related work: Builds on design RFC ENG-4719 and is the private-installer complement to the runtime nodeclass model in redwood (ENG-4592). Migration work item tracked in Linear ENG-4821; support ticket SUP-3217 covers customer migration requests.

Notes: This PR deliberately keeps changes additive and provides feature flags to fall back to the previous shared behavior. Operators upgrading private installs must coordinate with SRE to schedule locks and migration windows. Detailed operator runbook and rollback steps included in docs/operators/tenant-migration.md (new file in this PR).

feat(terraform): add iam_credential_broker module and broker controller manifest
tools: add state_partitioner Go CLI with dry-run and rollback modes
docs: add operator runbook for tenant state partitioning and migration
tests: add acceptance tests for nodeclass allocation and broker rotation
chore(lint): fix module variable names flagged by terraform-lint
review_comments: Samuel Kerr: Pulled a quick pass. High level looks good. Two asks: (1) can the state_partitioner detect resources with missing tenant tags and fail loudly instead of heuristics? (2) prefer rotate_interval variable default to 24h not 1h.

Diego Martinez: Reply: good catches. Added a --strict mode to state_partitioner which rejects ambiguous resources and updated rotate_interval default to 24h. See commits: tools: add strict mode and update broker defaults.
Ava Patel: Approving after verifying tests in staging and reviewing the operator runbook. Left a nit about documenting the Vault integration path in more detail.
Priya Nair: Requested change: reference to HSM integrations should be optional in module params. Diego: made the KMS/HSM toggle optional and documented it.
CI Bot: terraform fmt failed on first run, then fixed in chore(lint) commit and re-run passed all checks.
